finding: Whether a KTuner CVT map has an active torque limiter is disputed. Owners say there is none ('a non-CVT tune is detuned to achieve less torque'; 'KTuner has no torque limit'), while KTuner refuses to say what it does to the torque tables and, fixing a low-rpm judder, said it was 're-introducing some limitations placed by the factory', none beyond factory.
basis: Contested: Forum (2 owners, no evidence) vs Primary-adjacent (KTuner on its own Starter software) + our research docs (torque-based ECU, downpipe-power-research.md §1)
kb_relation: contradicts kc-cvt; contradicts kc-power-sources; contradicts kc-table-boost (forum side only)
ktuner_setting: none exposed (factory torque limiter); Starter maps
log_channel: TPS vs TPS Command, Turbo Pressure Target vs table, on a floored held pull
notes: Better basis: the cards' side. KTuner says its Starter software keeps factory limitations, and both owner statements are opinions about secret tables (10th gen, 2019-2021). What would settle it on our car is the §2 floored pull: TPS Command held under the pedal or a target flat below 21 with Knock Control at the floor and VSA quiet is a factory cap at work. Either way the app makes no map change, so the cards keep their wording; this is a 'don't repeat' for the owner claim.

finding: A protection that limits airflow (Cylinder Fill Limitation, the torque cap, or a partial-support ECU bug) acts by closing the throttle, so it shows in a log as TPS Command dropping or sitting under the pedal while the pedal is held; a cap on the boost target instead shows as a flat target with the throttle wide open. Owners saw both: a partially supported non-Si CVT 'pulled the throttle back under load' on Starter 21, and EU CVT ECUs held TPS Command at 90-95 % with the target 2-3 psi short (100 % in ECO).
basis: Physics (torque-based drive-by-wire: fill and torque limits are enforced through the throttle plate) + Forum (T2 owner logs; the reply in 21584 is most likely KTuner staff but unsigned)
ktuner_setting: Cylinder Fill Limitation; Final Boost Target (no edit)
log_channel: TPS, TPS Command, Turbo Pressure Target, Turbo Pressure, EWG Position, VSA state
notes: This is the reading key for the 19.2 psi test in ktuner-community-knowledge.md §2: floored and held, VSA off and no slip. (a) TPS Command under about 99 while TPS stays at its stop: a protection is closing the throttle. (b) TPS Command 99-100 and the target flat below 21: the target itself is capped. (c) Target reaches 21: a Boost step can be considered. (a) and (b) are both 'no map change'. VSA can also drop TPS Command (engine follow-up 7), so a pull with a slip event doesn't count. civicx-154 and civicx-66 (EU ECU, ECO reaching 100 %) are counted in g1-boost-05; our car reached TPS Command 99-100, so (a) is not yet seen here.

finding: KTuner (10th-gen base 1.5T): Starter tops out at 21 psi because that is 'the safe point for the CVT and factory clutch', and the base engine's rods are weaker than the Si's; independent testing put Hondata's '+9' about equal to KTuner's 21 psi in power, and more boost with less timing can make less power. KTuner also reads the factory target as 13.6 psi at 4,000 rpm and 14.6 at 5,000, peaking near 16 only at 5,500.
basis: Primary (KTuner on its own maps; unsigned post whose content is KTuner speaking: "we chose", "our 21PSI")
kb_relation: contradicts kc-boost-step (its 22-23.4 psi steps go past KTuner's own CVT safe point); confirms kc-expectations
log_channel: none (mechanical margin; no log shows rod or CVT stress)
notes: Caveat: said for the 10th gen; KTuner's 22+ Civic CVT Starter maps also stop at 21, so the choice carried over. Replaces civicx-50 (unsupported: not in its thread) as the source for 'KTuner chose 21 psi as a safe limit' in g1-boost-04. The Boost step play gates on logs (pedal, overshoot, timing, knock, fuel pressure), but this margin is the CVT, clutch and rods, which no log gate measures. Our map already sits at that point; the wastegate at 2.5 % open says there is little left anyway (kc-expectations). Needs an owner decision: keep the Boost step at all, or cap it at 21.

finding: Forum advice: 'if you see STFT adding 20% fuel … adjust the maf scaling g/s by -20%'.
basis: Physics + Primary (KTuner staff and owners in kc-maf-trim-direction: a positive trim means the sensor under-reads air, so g/s goes up)
ktuner_setting: MAF Scaling (AFM Flow on the 11th gen)
log_channel: STFT B1, LTFT B1 by airflow point
notes: Sign is backwards: added fuel means the ECU saw too little air for the oxygen it measured, so the curve must read more air at that point. Followed literally it doubles the error. Posted on a 2.0 NA thread (T3), but the advice is platform-generic, so keep it as a never-say. Fit: the thread car is not ours, but the method applies to any KTuner MAF Scaling edit, so it is kept as a never-say for this car.

finding: Owner claim (T2, Phearable 1.5): fuel trims lock at 0 as soon as the car enters boost, 'even at 1psi'.
basis: Data (this car: STFT B1 exactly 0 on 28-30 % of warm rows at 0-4 psi, 16 % at 4-6, 43 % at 6-8, 89 % at 8-10, 99-100 % from 10 psi; 2,266 rows at 0-8 psi; cruise rows read 17-25 %)
notes: On this car low boost behaves like cruise; trims freeze only from about 8 psi, as both cards say. The other T2 owner (civicx-233, MAPerformance intake on an Si) saw STFT move as soon as boost came, which matches ours. The 6-8 psi bin is already 43 % frozen, so the engine's 'drop rows with STFT exactly 0' rule matters more than the 8 psi line there.

finding: One owner (10th gen, 2020-era TunerView) says the TunerView CSV log doesn't carry MAF voltage, though the KTuner app shows it live.
kb_relation: extends kc-log-gate; extends kc-drive-brief (risk to their MAF Hz ask)
log_channel: MAF Hz (AFM Hz) column in the exported CSV
notes: Our logger already lacks MAF Hz (kc-log-channels). If TunerView can't export it at all, the log gate's 'MAF Hz in the gauge list' can never pass and every log would read short. 10th-gen non-Si MAF is in volts, ours in Hz, and TunerView has changed since, so this may not apply. Settle: owner opens the TunerView gauge list and looks for an airflow-frequency gauge, logs it a minute, exports, and checks for the column. Until then treat missing MAF Hz as Can't tell for the headroom check, never as a failed log.

finding: With the ECO button on, the car keeps Honda's stock ECO behaviour whatever psi the ECO table holds: duller throttle response and reduced A/C output. So the ECO tune is the reduced-power setup, and the strong tune belongs on ECO off.
basis: Forum (1 T2 owner, experienced) + Honda ECON design (ECON also eases climate control; not in our ground truth)
ktuner_setting: Boost Target ECO; ECO Button options (Factory ECO Control / Normalized ECO)
notes: Matters here: kc-dual-boost-targets tells the owner to use ECO on hot days and in traffic, and in Vietnamese heat a weaker A/C is a real cost. KTuner's 'Normalized ECO' option (g1-thr-15) keeps ECO's economy traits but makes it feel like Normal; whether it restores A/C output is not stated. Owner check: does the A/C feel weaker in ECO on this car?
